Found the bug: in TruncateStringFilter.process, the condition is inverted. It currently skips truncation for String.Single tokens (the actual string literals) and falls through to truncate everything else, including identifiers — exactly matching the reported regression (truncates identifiers instead of strings, and doesn't truncate actual string literals). Fixing the condition to `!=` so only String.Single literals get truncated and everything else passes through unchanged.
